Laura / Ben — I reviewed the supplied docs. Notes below (summary, not legal advice):

- Vendor VAT status: Skybridge appears VAT-registered in Ukraine (VATIN UA12345678). The attached certificate looks legitimate though procurement/legal may want the notarized extract for our records.

- VAT treatment for non-resident SaaS: Generally, when a non-resident supplies electronic services to a business that is registered for VAT in another jurisdiction, Ukrainian VAT is not typically charged to the foreign business (the supplier may zero-rate export of services). However, Ukrainian rules can differ by supply type and whether the buyer has a Ukrainian VAT presence.

- Reverse charge: For services supplied to a Ukrainian VAT payer, reverse charge applies. For non-resident supplier invoicing a foreign buyer (Redwood Inference EU B.V.), Skybridge may treat the supply as export (zero-rated). We need a written confirmation from Skybridge on whether they will treat Redwood as a non-Ukrainian customer and issue zero-rated invoices.

- PO routing recommendation: To avoid Ukrainian withholding or local registration complications, route the PO and invoice to Redwood Inference EU B.V. (EU legal entity). Finance should provide the legal name and VAT ID to include on the vendor invoice.

- Invoice fields to capture: Vendor VAT number, buyer entity name + VAT (if available), statement on VAT ("VAT not charged — export of services" or "Reverse charge applies"), and bank BIC/SWIFT.

Action items for vendor from our side:
- Please confirm whether you will issue invoices without Ukrainian VAT (export of services) to Redwood Inference EU B.V., or whether you expect to charge Ukrainian VAT.
- If you require any buyer-side declaration, indicate the exact language.

I've dropped a short draft note (redwood_ukr_tax_note_draft.pdf) for Procurement/Finance to include in the vendor file.

Karthik
Senior Tax Counsel
Redwood Inference
